scope: Cosmos-backed assistant-origin diagnostic for the six assistant-extraction experiment cases.
conclusions: Normal assistant extraction fixed two cases where gold evidence reached top-k: cc539528 and 8464fc84.

Three remaining misses had no lexical gold evidence found in the full canonical fact store under accent-insensitive phrase checks: 1de5cff2, 6ae235be, dc439ea3. Treat these as candidate extraction/storage misses, not proven semantic absence.

One remaining miss is a likely retrieval/ranking miss under lexical store inspection: 70b3e69b had both Manolo and Garcia evidence somewhere in the fact store but not top-k. Confirm same-fact co-occurrence or run larger recall before making runtime changes.
caveats: Needle checks are lexical diagnostics over gold strings, not runtime behavior. They are offline-only and must not be used by runtime extraction/retrieval/answering.
The lexical-not-found bucket means gold phrases were not found in fact_text or metadata. It can still miss paraphrases, so extraction prompt changes require relaxed/semantic inspection first.

The diagnostic required a temporary Cosmos public-access/IP-rule window; after inspection, Cosmos was restored to publicNetworkAccess Enabled with empty ipRules and AzureServices bypass, and API readiness returned OK.
next_steps: Run relaxed semantic/embedding or manual inspection for the three lexical-not-found cases before changing extraction prompts.
Run larger recall/top_k or assistant-origin retrieval gating for 70b3e69b before prompt changes.
Run full flag-off/flag-on regression before adopting assistant extraction broadly.
